content.user_title: Build Local AI with the Chrome Prompt API
content.value_statement: Browser AI projects require careful handling of availability, sessions, quotas, and model downloads. This guide provides practical Prompt API patterns for reliable local features.
actual_capabilities: Explains Prompt API availability checks, parameters, and session creation.
Demonstrates streaming, cancellation, cloning, cleanup, and quota tracking.
Shows text, image, and audio input configuration.
Uses JSON Schema constraints for predictable structured responses.
Covers permission policies, Chrome extensions, local development, and error handling.
limitations: The guide targets supported desktop Chrome versions and excludes mobile browsers.
Gemini Nano requires substantial storage, memory, and an initial model download.
Prompt API support varies by Chrome version, origin trial, language, and modality.
Examples require adaptation, testing, and validation before production use.

use_cases.title: Prototype Browser AI
use_cases.description: Create local summarization, classification, or extraction features with availability checks and streaming responses.

use_cases.title: Add Extension Intelligence
use_cases.description: Integrate Prompt API sessions into Chrome extensions while handling permissions, errors, and model readiness.

use_cases.title: Design Private Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan offline and privacy-sensitive processing with local sessions, structured output, and multimodal inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Support
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a minimal Prompt API availability check and explain every possible status.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Reliable Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Prompt API session with download progress, cancellation, parameter limits, and clear error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Return Structured Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a constrained response plan for extracting three validated hashtags from user text.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multimodal Session Recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multimodal workflow with image input, streaming, quota monitoring, session restoration, cloning, and cleanup.

output_examples.input: Explain how to prepare a session before prompting.
output_examples.output: Check matching availability options, monitor any download, create the session after user activation, and handle unsupported configurations.

output_examples.input: Recommend a pattern for long generated responses.
output_examples.output: Use streaming, expose a stop control through AbortController, track quota usage, and destroy unused sessions.
Define a strict response schema, request constrained output, parse the result, and validate it before application use.

best_practices: Check availability with the same options used for session creation.
Provide cancellation, monitor quota usage, and release unused sessions.
Validate constrained responses before using them in application logic.
anti_patterns: Do not assume the model is downloaded or available.
Do not store sensitive conversation history without explicit data controls.
Do not rely on unconstrained model text for structured application decisions.

faq.question: Does this skill run AI models itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance for Chrome's browser-managed Gemini Nano Prompt API.

faq.question: Which platforms are supported?
faq.answer: The guide targets eligible desktop Chrome environments. Mobile Chrome and unsupported ChromeOS devices are excluded.

faq.question: Can the API accept images and audio?
faq.answer: Yes, supported configurations can accept text, image, and audio inputs. Output remains text.

faq.question: How can responses be made predictable?
faq.answer: Pass a JSON Schema response constraint, parse the result, and validate it before use.

faq.question: Does model download require user interaction?
faq.answer: Yes. Model download requires active user activation, such as a click, tap, or key press.

faq.question: Can sessions be restored after restart?
faq.answer: The guide shows storing parameters and conversation history locally, then recreating a session with initial prompts.
